jobDescription:
Cloud Support Engineer — Enterprise Support (AWS)

You are the person an enterprise customer reaches when their production workload on AWS is broken. You own the case from first contact to resolution: reproducing the problem, reading the logs, forming a hypothesis, and either resolving it with the customer or escalating it to the service team with enough evidence that they can act on it.

What the role requires:
- Hands-on diagnosis, not case routing. You will read CloudTrail, CloudWatch, VPC flow logs and IAM policies yourself, and form your own hypothesis before anyone else looks.
- Judgment about escalation: knowing when a problem is a customer misconfiguration, when it is a service limit, and when it is a genuine product defect worth paging a service team.
- Direct written and spoken communication with enterprise customers under pressure, including during an active Sev-1, without a manager translating.
- A clear account of your own incident role: whether you drove the bridge, owned customer communications, or contributed a specific diagnosis.

How we evaluate:
We do not weight titles or team metrics. We weight what you personally diagnosed, what you decided to escalate and why, and which numbers are yours rather than your queue's.

answers:
Q: Describe a production incident you worked on. What did you personally do?

A: Last year one of our largest enterprise accounts had an outage that took down their checkout path for about three hours. I was on the case from the start and worked it through to resolution. We looked at everything — networking, permissions, the database layer — and eventually got them back up. The customer was very happy with how we handled it and it came up again in their renewal call.

Q: How do you decide when to escalate?

A: I escalate when it is clear the issue is beyond what I can resolve directly. I try to make sure the service team has what they need when I hand it over. I have worked closely with service teams on a number of tricky issues.

Q: What does the CSAT number on your resume represent?

A: It reflects the quality of support we delivered over a sustained period. Enterprise customers are demanding, and keeping them satisfied at that level takes real consistency.

Q: Why this role?

A: I want to go deeper on the diagnosis side. A lot of my current queue is well-understood issues where the answer is already in a runbook, and I would rather spend my time on the problems where nobody knows the answer yet.
